text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Thursday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- A Vilnius court postponed the trial of a suspected organised crime boss Henrikas Daktaras after one of his defence attorneys was sent to hospital. Daktaras might be sentenced to 10 years imprisonment if found guilty.
- After five years of talks Lithuanian lawmakers are expected to vote for the law on national security. Lithuania was the only Baltic country which had no law of this kind.

- The new government is looking for revenue sources for the 1997 budget. Finance Minister Rolandas Matiliauskas has suggested the imposition of dividend taxes on state-owned companies and to increase taxes on real estate from one to 1.5 percent to add 150 million litas to the budget. Another 150 million litas is expected to be collected by tougher anti-contraband actions.
- A colonel of of the U.S. Army, Romas Kulikauskas, has been suggested as the head of the border police.
- Demand exceeded supply for the global depository receipts issue worth $6.0 million by the leading dairy firm Birzai Milk.
- A year has passed since Innovation Bank was closed but its fate remains unclear. The new government has postponed concrete decisions to February.

- Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius said in an interview on relations with industry that one of the main reasons a member of the Confederation of Industrialists was appointed as economy minister was the hope that industrialists can reform the energy sector best.
